products.title: RWANDA, Rugali CWS, Nyamasheke
products.body_html:
Producer: Muraho Trading Co. 

Growing altitude: 1600-1800m above sea level.

Botanical variety: Bourbon.

Process: Natural.

Tasting notes: Molasses, raspberry, passion fruit, cranberry flavours.

Roast date: 27 August, 2026

The road from Kigali to Rugali is one of Rwanda’s most stunning drives. Winding through the verdant Nyamasheke District, travelers pass rolling hills, dense forests, vibrant villages, and thriving coffee farms—until the landscape opens up to reveal the shimmering expanse of Lake Kivu, Rwanda’s largest lake and a natural border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Set on the shores of Lake Kivu and surrounded by Rwanda’s iconic thousand hills, Rugali Coffee Washing Station (CWS) is more than a processing site—it’s a cultural and agricultural hub.

Though Rugali CWS is still relatively young, it has grown into one of the most respected and community-centered stations in Rwanda. This success is thanks to the tireless work of the Muraho Trading Co. team and the many smallholder farmers who make up the extended Rugali family.

95% of coffee trees in Rwanda are Bourbon, and Rugali’s lots show why. Rich sweetness, a structured body, and clarity in the cup.

Rwanda’s coffee industry is unique: No large estates. Over 400,000 smallholders, each owning less than a quarter hectare

Cooperative models and community-run stations form the backbone of production. Rugali and its sister station Kilimbi made history as the first washing stations in Rwanda legally permitted to produce and export Natural and Honey-processed coffees—paving the way for innovation across the country.

“Through our relationship with Muraho and the families behind Rugali, we’re able to showcase the beauty, resilience, and potential of Rwanda’s smallholder coffee.”

products.title: INDONESIA, Wildan & Fikri Mustafa, Frinsa Estate, Pangalengan, Java
products.body_html:
Producer: Wildan & Fikri Mustafa. 

Growing altitude: 1400m above sea level.

Botanical variety: Ateng Super.

Process: Natural Ext. Fermentation, Lactobacillus Cerevisiae.

Tasting notes: Dark chocolate, plum, passion fruit, blackberry, mandarin flavours.

Roast date: PLEASE NOTE!!! This coffee is roasted on demand, so please keep in mind it will take longer to ship. 

Wildan Mustofa and his wife, Atieq Mustikaningtyas, embarked on their first coffee project in the Sindangkerta, Weninggalih area back in 2010, which eventually evolved into Java Frinsa Estate. Their commitment to quality set them apart, as they focused on fully washed coffees while most Indonesian producers opted for wet-hulled methods, even within the specialty coffee market.

Frinsa Estate is situated in West Java, known locally as Sunda. With a wet mill, well-ventilated storage space, and dry mill, all located at an altitude of 1400masl, they have complete control over their product, from harvest to grading, sorting, and shipment. The estate encompasses six main growing plots across the region, including; Weninggalih, Mekarwangi, Tilu Mountain, Pengalengan, Malabar Mountain, Garut.

They also source cherries from selected outgrowers in the area. The resulting coffees are marketed under the name of Frinsa Collective.

While most of their coffees undergo the fully washed process, Frinsa Estate also produces some wet-hulled and natural coffees, primarily catering to the local market. The estate meticulously separates their coffees into distinct lots based on field location, cultivar, and picking date.

The Ateng Super coffee variety is a cultivar originating from the Gayo Highlands in Aceh, Sumatra, Indonesia. It is a locally developed selection of the Catimor variety, specifically bred to enhance productivity and disease resistance.

The process of this coffee is a controlled fermentation using Lactobacillus and Cerevisiae, where bacteria and yeast work together to enhance sweetness, soften acidity, and create a more complex, rounded cup.

Additionally, in collaboration with the coffee research centre, Frinsa Estate has undertaken extensive cultivation of various unknown cultivars, segregating them into designated blocks within the farm. Given the relative youth of the farm and trees, the flavour profiles of many of these cultivars are still being discovered. Apart from their own coffee production, Frinsa Estate also processes coffee for local smallholders, typically sorting them by area.

products.title: ETHIOPIA, Hambella, West Guji, Oromia
products.body_html:
Producer: Faysel Abdosh. 

Growing altitude: 1900-2200m above sea level.

Botanical variety: Ethiopian Heirloom.

Process: Natural Anaerobic.

Tasting notes: Honey, plum, blueberry, jasmine, bergamot flavours.

Roast date: 27 August, 2026

Nestled in the highlands of West Guji, Ethiopia, the Hambella region has earned a reputation for producing some of the country’s most expressive and sought-after coffees. Rich volcanic soils, elevations reaching over 2,000 metres, and a cool climate create ideal conditions for slow cherry maturation, resulting in exceptional sweetness and complexity.

This coffee is produced by Testi Coffee Company, one of Ethiopia’s leading specialty coffee exporters, renowned for their commitment to quality, innovation, and long-term relationships with farming communities. Cherries are carefully hand-picked at peak ripeness before undergoing an anaerobic natural fermentation, where they are fermented in sealed tanks with limited oxygen. This controlled process enhances fruit intensity and aromatic complexity while preserving the distinct character of the origin.

Following fermentation, the cherries are slowly dried on raised African beds under carefully monitored conditions until they reach the ideal moisture content. The result is a vibrant and layered cup that showcases both the remarkable terroir of West Guji and Testi Coffee’s meticulous approach to processing.

This lot has also been classified as Ethiopian Grade 1, the country’s highest green coffee quality designation. Achieving Grade 1 requires exceptionally careful processing and sorting to minimise physical defects while delivering outstanding cup quality. Every stage, from cherry selection and drying to milling and hand-sorting is meticulously managed to ensure only the finest beans are exported. While a Grade 1 classification does not define flavour on its own, it reflects the highest standards of preparation and consistency, providing a strong foundation for an exceptional cup.

Expect a coffee bursting with ripe berry sweetness, tropical fruit notes, and floral jasmine and lavender aromatics, balanced by a silky body and a lingering, wine-like finish. It is an expressive example of modern Ethiopian coffee processing while remaining unmistakably rooted in the unique landscape of Hambella.

“Every harvest is an opportunity to reveal what our farmers and our land are capable of. Our role is simply to preserve that potential and allow the coffee to tell its own story.”

—  Faysel Abdosh, Testi Coffee Company

products.title: COSTA RICA, Pie San, San Lorenzo, Tarrazú
products.body_html:
Producer: Luis & Oscar Monge. 

Growing altitude: 1900-2000m above sea level.

Botanical variety: Geisha.

Process: Red Honey.

Tasting notes: Chocolate, rose water, cranberry, orange rind flavours.

Roast date: PLEASE NOTE!!! This coffee is roasted on demand, so please keep in mind it will take longer to ship. 

Produced by the Monge family at La Lia Beneficio in the celebrated coffee-growing region of Tarrazú, Costa Rica, this Geisha represents the marriage of one of the world's most sought-after coffee varieties with one of Costa Rica's signature processing methods.

Since establishing Beneficio La Lia in 2007, the Monge family has become one of Costa Rica’s most respected specialty coffee producers. Their meticulous approach to cultivation and processing has earned repeated recognition in the prestigious Costa Rica Cup of Excellence, the country’s highest competition for quality coffee. Over the years, coffees from La Lia have achieved numerous Cup of Excellence placements. Their pursuit of quality continues today, with Geisha lots from La Lia once again featuring amongst Costa Rica’s highest-scoring coffees in recent Cup of Excellence competitions. 

Originally discovered in the forests of Ethiopia and later cultivated in Panama, the Geisha variety has earned an international reputation for its extraordinary elegance and complexity. Rather than relying on body or intensity, Geisha captivates with refined floral aromatics, delicate tea-like characteristics and remarkable clarity in the cup. When grown at high elevations and carefully processed, it reveals vibrant layers of citrus, tropical fruit and jasmine-like florals that have made it one of the most celebrated varieties in specialty coffee.

To complement the elegance of the variety, the Monge family processes this coffee using the traditional Costa Rican Red Honey method. Despite its name, no honey is added during processing. Instead, after the cherries are depulped, a generous layer of the fruit's natural sugars (mucilage) is intentionally left on the parchment while the coffee dries. As the mucilage slowly dries, those sugars contribute additional sweetness, a silky mouthfeel and greater complexity, while still preserving the clean, vibrant character for which Costa Rican coffees are renowned.

The result is a beautifully balanced coffee that captures both the unmistakable elegance of Geisha and the sweetness of the Red Honey process. Expect expressive floral aromas, notes of jasmine, ripe yellow tropical fruits, citrus and honeyed sweetness, finishing with a refined tea-like delicacy that lingers long after the final sip.

products.title: ETHIOPIA, Alemayehu Daniel, Gedeb, Yirgacheffe
products.body_html:
Producer: Alemayehu Daniel.

Growing altitude: 1800-2000m above sea level.

Botanical variety: Ethiopian heirloom.

Process: Natural.

Tasting notes: Honey, jasmine, watermelon, pineapple, citrus, raspberry flavours. 

Roast date: 27 August, 2026

Back in 2011, a new movement began in Yirgacheffe. Small and medium farmers were encouraged to step out from under the shadow of the large cooperatives by investing in their own processing and drying facilities. For the first time, producers could take full control of their coffee, picking only the ripest cherries, processing with care, and drying with precision. This shift gave rise to a generation of farmers able to craft their own microlots, elevating both quality and identity.

Yirgacheffe is renowned for its complex, floral, and citrus-driven coffees, grown at altitudes reaching 2,000 meters above sea level. Traditionally, cherries from across the region were blended together at cooperative mills. But with the advent of small private micro-mills, we now have the privilege to taste coffees that tell the story of a single farm, a single family, and a single vision.

One such story belongs to Alemayehu. His grandfather established the family farm in 1946, planting it with coffee trees from Kochere. Since 1998, Alemayehu has carried on this legacy with a hands-on approach, dedicating himself to nurturing both the land and his community.

This particular lot is naturally processed: cherries are carefully picked and laid out on raised African beds, turned every few hours to ensure even drying. Over six to eight weeks, the fruit slowly transforms under the Ethiopian sun, developing the clarity and depth that Yirgacheffe is famous for. Once dried to perfection, the coffee is hulled, sorted, and prepared for export with meticulous attention.

When we first visited Alemayehu’s farm, we were welcomed not just by his coffee but by his family’s warmth and generosity. It was one of the most heart-warming experiences in our sourcing journey and cemented our commitment to support Alemayehu and his community well beyond that first visit.

This cup is more than just coffee, it is heritage, dedication, and the future of independent farming in Yirgacheffe.

“For many years, I dreamed of being able to process and share my own coffee, but it felt impossible without the support of partners who believed in me.

Working together has given me the chance not only to grow better coffee, but to create a future for my family and opportunities for my community.

Every bag of coffee that leaves my farm carries our story, our hard work, and our gratitude.” - Alemayehu Daniel

products.title: COSTA RICA, Alejo Castro Khale, Volcán Azul Reserve, Valle Centrale
products.body_html:
Producer: Alejo Castro-Kahle. 

Growing altitude: 1700masl. 

Botanical variety: Geisha.

Process: Natural Anaerobic.

Tasting notes: Syrup, apricot, blackberry, vanilla, hibiscus, passion fruit flavours.

Roast date: PLEASE NOTE!!! This coffee is roasted on demand, so please keep in mind it will take longer to ship. 

There are coffees that speak of place, and then there are coffees that become the place. Volcán Azul’s Geisha sits firmly in the latter category, a coffee that embodies the altitude, history, and quiet ambition of one of Costa Rica’s most storied estates. That vision was recognised on the world stage as Volcán Azul’s Geisha earned 4th place in the Cup of Excellence, reaffirming its position among the most exceptional coffees on the planet.

For those who know the farm, this achievement feels less like a surprise and more like a continuation of a legacy. Volcán Azul’s philosophy has always been rooted in precision: meticulous picking, intentional processing, and a deep respect for the land that sustains it. Geisha, with its delicate florals, luminous sweetness, and almost weightless clarity, is the variety through which this philosophy shines brightest.

In the cup, the 4th-place Geisha is a quiet revelation, jasmine and white florals lifted by stone fruit and citrus, finishing with the kind of clean, crystalline aftertaste that defines world-class coffee. But beyond the sensory experience lies something more enduring: the decades-long commitment of the Castro family to elevate Costa Rican coffee, season after season, through both heritage and experimentation.

For us at Espressolab, celebrating this recognition is personal. Volcán Azul is not just a supplier, it is a partner whose pursuit of excellence mirrors our own. To share this coffee with our guests is to share a piece of Costa Rica’s finest craftsmanship, shaped by volcanic soils, mountain winds, and human devotion.

Congratulations to Volcán Azul on this remarkable achievement. Fourth place in the Cup of Excellence is not merely a ranking, it is proof that exceptional coffee is born from a harmony between land, variety, producer, and purpose.

“Quality coffee and conservation go hand in hand—this is the future we’re cultivating, one harvest at a time.”

— Alejo Castro Kahle

products.title: NICARAGUA, Erwin  Miersich, Los Placeres, Yasica Sur, Matagalpa
products.body_html:
Producer: Erwin Miersich & family. 

Growing altitude: 1200m above sea level.

Botanical variety: Ethiosar.

Process: Natural Anaerobic.

Tasting notes: Caramel, papaya, blood orange, cherry, hibiscus flavours.

Roast date: 27 August, 2026

Fincas Miersich is a distinguished network of farms located across Nicaragua, including; Limoncillo, Las Delicias, San Jose, Los Placeres, La Huella, Mama Mina, Cerro Azul, La Escondida, Los Altos, Suspiro, and Milagros.

Together, they form a unified vision led by one of Nicaragua’s most hardworking and forward-thinking coffee families.

In the political upheaval of the 1980s, the Miersich family lost everything. Their land was seized, and they were forced into exile—rebuilding their lives abroad, primarily in North America, but their connection to Nicaragua and its soil never wavered.

When the opportunity came, they returned to reclaim their land, and with it, a new purpose: to build a sustainable coffee legacy that would never be uprooted again.

Today, the Miersich family manages their farms with a strong commitment to environmental stewardship and social responsibility.

Their initiatives include reducing water usage and pollution, preventing soil erosion, minimizing on-farm waste, improving living and working conditions for all staff. 

Their operations often support up to 300 workers, to whom they provide free education for children aged 5–10. Free daycare for infants.

Led by Dr. Miersich, Erwin, Steve, and Erwin Jr., the family continually pushes the boundaries of coffee cultivation and processing. Their experimental and varietal work includes processing methods, anaerobic fermentation, cold fermentation, and varietals planted Geisha, Ethiosar, Javanica, Yellow Pacamara, and others. 

Each farm serves as a living laboratory, producing exceptional microlots while refining techniques that balance quality and sustainability.

Coffee remains central to Nicaragua’s economy and cultural fabric. With around 40,000 families relying on coffee production for their livelihoods, the work of the Miersich family represents not just personal restoration—but also a broader contribution to rural stability and progress.

“We returned not just to grow coffee, but to grow a future—for our family, our land, and our people.”

— The Miersich Family

products.title: COSTA RICA, Alejo Castro Khale, Volcán Azul, Valle Centrale
products.body_html:
Producer: Alejo Castro-Kahle. 

Growing altitude: 1700masl. 

Botanical variety: Typica.

Process: Natural Warm Anaerobic.

Tasting notes: Maple syrup, mandarin, pineapple, lime, red currant flavours.

Roast date: 27 August, 2026

Volcán Azul is a family-run coffee farm operated by Alejo Castro Kahle, alongside his father Fernando Castro Jiménez and mother Vivian Kahle. Both branches of the family trace their coffee-growing heritage in Costa Rica back to the 1800s. For the past 15 years, they have jointly managed the Volcán Azul micro-mill, producing some of the purest and most distinctive coffees in the world.

Set on the fertile slopes of Poás Volcano at elevations above 1,500 meters, the farm benefits from rich volcanic soil and an ideal microclimate. This Strictly Hard Bean (SHB) environment nurtures exceptional flavor development from planting to harvest.

Each step in their process reflects precision and care: Selective planting of high-quality varieties. Meticulous processing at the on-site micro-mill. Strict sorting and preparation for export-grade beans.

The family’s mission goes beyond quality. Descendants of Don Alejo C. and Don Wilhelm have expanded their legacy by championing environmental conservation as a core value. Since the 1980s, they have actively acquired over 1,500 hectares of rainforest in coffee-growing areas and the Osa Peninsula, one of the most biodiverse regions on Earth (home to 2.5% of global biodiversity).

By protecting natural rainforest ecosystems, they aim to reduce global warming, air contamination, and preserve critical biodiversity for generations to come.

We are proud to work with F.C.J. Volcán Azul, a family whose deep-rooted expertise, environmental ethics, and vision for the future align with the highest standards in specialty coffee.

Their coffees embody the harmony between agronomic excellence and ecological responsibility—each cup a reflection of volcanic terroir, meticulous craftsmanship, and a legacy of stewardship.

“Quality coffee and conservation go hand in hand—this is the future we’re cultivating, one harvest at a time.”

— Alejo Castro Kahle

products.title: HONDURAS, Moises & Marysabel Caballero, Xichlete, Chinacla, La Paz
products.body_html:
Producer: Marysabel & Moises Caballero.

Growing altitude: 1600m above sea level.

Botanical variety: Catuaí.

Process: Natural Extended Fermentation.

Tasting notes: Molasses, passion fruit, banana, apricot, basil, guava flavours.

Roast date: 27 August, 2026

In the coffee-rich region of Marcala, Honduras, Marysabel Caballero and her husband Moises Herrera, along with Marysabel’s father Don Fabio Caballero, manage over 200 hectares of coffee farmland. This is not just a family business—it’s a generational story of resilience, innovation, and an unwavering pursuit of quality.

Don Fabio, one of the early pioneers of Honduran coffee cultivation, inherited vast tracts of land from his father. After facing years of low returns, he entrusted key parcels to his children—particularly Marysabel and Moises. Moises, already a coffee farmer himself, added his farms to the family operation. Today, their combined holdings span 17 distinct farms, each meticulously managed and documented.

The Caballeros have earned international recognition for their dedication to quality. Consistent high rankings in the Cup of Excellence, one of the few producers from their area to do so regularly

Their focus on quality spans every detail—from cherry selection to processing, from soil health to varietal experimentation.

Sustainability is more than a goal—it’s a way of life on the Caballero farms. They are deeply committed to soil regeneration and biodiversity, producing their own organic compost using Cow and chicken manure, coffee pulp, local organic matter. 

This is complemented by minimal use of mineral fertilizers to ensure their coffee trees receive the full spectrum of nutrients needed for resilience and cup quality.

In addition to coffee, the farms grow oranges, avocados, bananas, and flowers—not for export, but to provide food for farm workers during harvest. Support biodiversity and shade-grown coffee practices and enhance the farm’s ecosystem and long-term sustainability.

Every process on the Caballero farms is carefully tracked and evaluated. From planting new varieties to investing in modern equipment, Marysabel and Moises embody a progressive and data-driven approach to coffee farming—balancing traditional knowledge with innovation.

Their success has not only elevated the reputation of their own farms but has also contributed significantly to Honduras’s rising status as a specialty coffee origin.

“We don’t just grow coffee—we grow opportunities, resilience, and community with every harvest.”

— Marysabel Caballero

products.title: COSTA RICA, Federico Castro Khale, Finca Colima Reserve, Valle Centrale
products.body_html:
Producer: Federico & Alejo Castro-Kahle. 

Growing altitude: 1400masl. 

Botanical variety: SL28.

Process: Washed.

Tasting notes: Caramel, lime zest, yellow plum, vanilla, pomelo, lemongrass fruit flavours.

Roast date: PLEASE NOTE!!! This coffee is roasted on demand, so please keep in mind it will take longer to ship. 

Some coffees don’t simply enter a competition, they arrive with a story, a lineage, and a level of craftsmanship that announces itself in the cup long before the scores are revealed. Hacienda Colima’s SL28 Washed did exactly that, earning an extraordinary second place in the 2025 Cup of Excellence, one of the most coveted accolades in the world of specialty coffee.

This achievement is more than a medal. It represents the culmination of years of intentional farming, disciplined processing, and relentless refinement and it places Hacienda Colima among the world’s most consistent producers of exceptional, competition-level lots.

The Cup of Excellence is widely regarded as the most rigorous and prestigious coffee competition globally. Coffees are scored blind by national and international juries through multiple elimination rounds, and only those that score above 87 points even qualify for the final stage  a threshold incredibly difficult for most coffees to cross.

To finish second is to stand at the very upper edge of global quality. It means this lot not only impressed but captivated a panel of judges known for their unyielding standards and experienced palates. It is confirmation that Hacienda Colima’s SL28 is not simply good; it is one of the world’s best coffees of the year.

The SL28 varietal, originally from Kenya, has long been celebrated for its expressive clarity and its ability to translate terroir with remarkable fidelity. At Hacienda Colima, this potential meets intentional cultivation, optimal elevation, rich volcanic soil, and a processing philosophy centred on purity.

The flavour profile is both classic and elevated: bright citrus notes layered over stone fruit sweetness, lifted by elegant florals and finishing with the kind of balance and length that only the finest washed SL28s can achieve. It is a coffee that feels both familiar and revelatory, rooted in tradition yet unmistakably shaped by its Costa Rican terroir.

For coffee lovers, this SL28 washed lot is a rare experience, one of those limited-auction coffees that remind us just how emotionally expressive and terroir-driven coffee can be. Whether brewed as a pour-over to reveal its high-tone clarity, or as a delicate, fruit-forward espresso, it offers a sensory journey that honours the farm, the variety, the soil, and the hands that shaped it.

In an industry often consumed by novelty, Hacienda Colima’s achievement stands as a reminder of what truly endures: mastery, patience, and devotion to craft. This SL28 Washed is not merely a competition coffee, it is a reflection of a farm at its peak, a celebration of origin, and a symbol of what is possible when passion and precision meet.

“Quality coffee and conservation go hand in hand—this is the future we’re cultivating, one harvest at a time.”

— Alejo Castro Kahle

products.title: GUATEMALA, Petrona Perez, Finca Satchibal, Huehuetenango
products.body_html:
Producer: Petrona Perez.

Growing altitude: 1800-2000m above sea level.

Botanical variety: Bourbon, Caturra.

Process: Washed.

Tasting notes: Syrup, medjool dates, tangerine, orange, blackcurrant flavours.

Roast date: 27 August, 2026

Petrona Perez and her mother manage their five-acre farm in the highlands of San Antonio Huista, standing as a powerful example of the vital role women play in coffee production.

Established in 2002, Finca Satchibal became entirely their responsibility after Petrona’s father left to seek work in North America. Mother and daughter have since managed every aspect of the farm themselves, overseeing the entire journey from hand-picking ripe coffee cherries to processing, drying, and delivering the finished parchment coffee to the exporter’s warehouse.

Their farm benefits from a unique microclimate shaped by dry, warm winds that sweep across the nearby Mexican border. Combined with the region’s high elevation, these conditions produce coffees with remarkable complexity, sweetness, and character that distinguish them within the region.

Driven by an unwavering desire to improve her craft, Petrona continually sought to deepen her understanding of coffee production and quality. Her determination eventually led her to our export partner, where she confidently presented a sample of her coffee, proudly declaring it to be among the finest in the region. The cupping results later proved her right.

Although Finca Satchibal is small and lacks the sophisticated infrastructure of many larger estates and mills, Petrona and her mother demonstrate that exceptional coffee is not defined by size, but by dedication, precision, and an uncompromising commitment to quality. Their meticulous attention to every detail is a reminder that extraordinary results can come from the humblest beginnings.

The name Satchibal translates to “the fruit of the tree,” a fitting reflection of the farm itself. More than simply producing exceptional coffee, it represents the fruits of years of perseverance, resilience, and determination as two independent women who have built a future through hard work and passion.

Coffee cultivation in Guatemala dates back to the 1850s and has long been a cornerstone of the country’s economy and agricultural heritage. For much of the 20th century and the early 21st century, Guatemala was Central America’s leading coffee producer before eventually being surpassed by neighbouring Honduras. Today, Guatemala remains internationally celebrated for its diverse growing regions, volcanic soils, and distinctive, high-quality coffees.

“Coffee has given my mother and me the opportunity to build something together. Every cup tells the story of our perseverance, our family, and the land we are fortunate to call home.” — Petrona Perez

products.title: PERU, Dreyde Perez Delgado, Chontali, Cajamarca
products.body_html:
Producer: Dreyde Perez Delgado. 

Growing altitude: 1950m above sea level.

Botanical variety: Geisha.

Process: Washed 72+72hr anaerobic.

Tasting notes: Molasses, jasmine, pomelo, cantaloupe, floral flavours.

Roast date: PLEASE NOTE!!! This coffee is roasted on demand, so please keep in mind it will take longer to ship. 

Peru is long celebrated among coffee lovers for its delicate, floral high-altitude arabicas, and nestled in the lush hills of Cajamarca, producer Dreyde Perez Delgado is making waves with his Geisha lots. 

Located in the district of Chontali, his farm is becoming known for Geisha that exemplifies what Peru can do at altitude, with clean processing and expressive flavour profiles. 

Altitude is one of the key factors: at nearly 2,000masl the cooler temperatures slow the maturation of beans, enhancing complexity, preserving acidity, and allowing more nuanced sugar development.

The 72+72 hour washed fermentation method lets the intrinsic qualities of the varietal and terroir shine through. In Delgado’s case, that seems to include floral notes, vibrant fruit, and clarity in acidity. 

What is the 72 + 72-Hour Fermentation. 

First, the whole cherries (i.e. before depulping) are fermented for 72 hours in an oxygen-free (anaerobic) tank. After that initial fermentation, the cherries are de-pulped (removing the pulp and mucilage) and then another 72 hours of fermentation occurs on the de-pulpedbeans.  

So overall, there’s 144 total hours of fermentation contact (72h in cherry + 72h post de-pulping).

Dreyde Perez Delgado’s “Ermelita” Geisha achieved 87.53 points in the 2023 Peru Cup of Excellence (COE). This score places his coffee among the top lots in the country suggesting both excellent quality and strong potential for specialty markets. Buyers and roasters are paying attention. 

When you taste Dreyde's Geisha, you are likely to encounter sweet, fruity flavours, pomelo, passion fruit, jasmine and a clean acidity. 

Geisha at high altitude in Cajamarca is a powerful combination: unique micro-climate, rich soils, excellent shade or shade-like conditions, and skilled post-harvest methods.

Getting over 87 points in COE is no small feat. It means consistent quality, careful picking (ripe cherries), proper fermentation, good washing, accurate drying, and good record-keeping. 

Dreyde's a small-scale producer. His size allows more attention to detail. It also means that his production is limited, which appeals to roasters and consumers wanting traceability and uniqueness.  

Dreyde Perez Delgado is one of the names in Peru that specialty coffee lovers around the world are watching. With his Geisha lots from Chontali, Cajamarca, he’s producing coffee that competes at high levels, shows beautiful complexity, and earns the kind of recognition that could help small producers build sustainable livelihoods.

products.title: RWANDA, Shyira CWS, Nyahibu
products.body_html:
Producer: Muraho Trading Co. 

Growing altitude: 1850-2300m above sea level.

Botanical variety: Bourbon.

Process: Washed.

Tasting notes: Molasses, blackberry, apricot, pomelo, rooibos flavours.

Roast date: 27 August, 2026

Shyira may be one of the smallest coffee washing stations, but it has one of the biggest personalities. Built in 2017, Shyira is the highest known coffee washing station in Rwanda, perched at 1,850 metres above sea level, with cherries sourced from farms reaching 2,300 metres. It is home to nearly 1,900 smallholder farming families, whose dedication produces some of the country’s most distinctive Red Bourbon coffees.  

An hour’s drive into the mountains from the township of Musanze (Ruhengeri), the journey itself is unforgettable. As the road climbs through Rwanda’s volcanic highlands, the landscape transforms into a breathtaking panorama of fertile volcanic soils, cool mountain air and dramatic ridgelines. These unique growing conditions slow the maturation of the coffee cherries, allowing them to develop exceptional sweetness, complexity and vibrant acidity.  

At the summit, you are rewarded with one of the most spectacular views in Rwanda. The majestic Virunga Volcanoes stretch across the horizon, forming the ancient home of the endangered Mountain Gorillas. Below, the Gicice River winds through valleys often blanketed by morning mist, while white sandy riverbeds, cascading waterfalls and endless green hills create a landscape that feels almost untouched by time.  

Despite its modest size, Shyira produces fully washed, honey and natural coffees, each expressing the remarkable character of this extraordinary terroir. Every harvest reminds us why altitude matters, and why coffees from Shyira consistently display remarkable elegance, clarity and longevity in the cup.  

It is often debated which of washing station is the most beautiful, Shyira, Kilimbi or Gisheke. The truth is, there is no winner. Each tells its own story. But once you’ve stood on the hills of Shyira, watched the clouds drift between the volcanoes and breathed in the cool mountain air, you’ll understand why so many quietly believe the “Little Baby” has something truly magical about it.

products.title: KENYA, Konyu, Kirinyanga
products.body_html:
Producer: Kabare Farmers Coop Society.

Growing altitude: 1800m above sea level.

Botanical variety: SL28, SL34.

Process: Washed.

Tasting notes: Syrup, blackcurrant, lime, earl grey, elderflower flavours.

Roast date: 27 August, 2026

Nestled on the fertile slopes of central Kenya, Kabare Farmers’ Cooperative Society (FCS) represents the collective strength of smallholder coffee farming at its finest. Serving as the central management body for eleven cooperatives — Kiringa, Konyu, Karani, Kiangombe, Kaboyo, Mukure, Mukengeria, Kimandi, Kathata, Kiangothe, and Kiamiciri — Kabare FCS unites nearly 10,000 farming households across Kirinyaga County.These farms stretch from the outskirts of Kerugoya town up toward the forested borders of Mount Kenya National Park, where altitude, climate, and soil converge to create ideal coffee-growing conditions.

Kirinyaga’s high elevations slow the maturation of coffee cherries. This extended ripening period allows sugars and organic acids to develop gradually, resulting in coffees known for their structure, vibrancy, and layered complexity. 

The region is particularly celebrated for its cultivation of SL-28 and SL-34, two historic Kenyan varieties prized for their bright, articulate acidity, blackcurrant and red berry notes, juicy sweetness, structured, wine-like depth.  

Combined with the area’s rich volcanic soils, these cultivars consistently produce coffees that are expressive and unmistakably Kenyan.

Within the Kabare FCS network, Konyu processing station, known locally as a “factory stands out with approximately 1,000 contributing farmer members.

On average, each smallholder farmer delivers around 250 kilograms of hand-picked cherry per harvest. After processing, this equates to roughly three-quarters of a single 60kg bag of exportable green coffee per farmer. While individually modest, collectively these contributions form significant, traceable community lots that reflect the shared effort of hundreds of families. 

Kabare Farmers’ Cooperative Society is more than an administrative body. It is a framework that allows thousands of smallholder farmers to access infrastructure, processing expertise, and global markets while maintaining individual farm ownership. 

The result is coffee that reflects both terroir and community, shaped by altitude, volcanic soil, traditional processing, and the disciplined work of nearly 10,000 farming households. 

From the slopes near Kerugoya to the forest edge of Mount Kenya, the story of Kabare FCS is one of collaboration, precision, and enduring commitment to quality, a reminder that exceptional coffee is rarely the work of one farm, but of many hands working together.

“Great coffee is never the work of one farm, but the shared effort of a community moving in the same direction.”  - Kabare Coop Society.

products.title: COLOMBIA, Sebastian Ramirez, El Placer, Quindio, Huila
products.body_html:
Producer: Sebastian Ramirez.

Growing altitude: 2100m above sea level.

Botanical variety: Pink Bourbon.

Process: Honey IPA.

Tasting notes: Molasses, pine, hops, mandarin, tropical fruit flavours. 

Roast date: 27 August, 2026

Sebastián Ramírez is a fourth-generation coffee producer from Quindío, Colombia, whose family has cultivated coffee for generations. Around 12 years ago, he turned his focus to specialty coffee, exploring fermentation, processing, and sensory development through innovative techniques that laid the foundation for El Placer Farms.

Today, Sebastián leads El Placer Farms, producing exceptional coffees through carefully controlled processing methods. From clean, classic profiles to more experimental fermentations, the project emphasizes quality, consistency, traceability, and balance. Located in Quindío, the farm benefits from volcanic soils, high elevations, and an ideal climate for slow cherry maturation. Alongside Pink Bourbon, the farm also cultivates varieties such as Geisha and Caturra.

El Placer coffees have earned international recognition, with Sebastián actively promoting collaboration and knowledge-sharing, believing that coffee is built on transparency, innovation, and strong producer relationships.

For this Pink Bourbon lot, only perfectly ripe cherries are selected before undergoing 100 hours of carbonic maceration in sealed CO₂ tanks. After depulping, while retaining the mucilage, the coffee is returned to sealed tanks for a further 100-hour fermentation with the addition of mosto, lemongrass, and hops to enhance aromatic complexity.

The coffee is then dried in mechanical dryers before finishing on raised African beds inside polytunnels, where carefully controlled airflow allows for slow, even drying and a stable final moisture content.

“Every coffee has its own identity. Our responsibility is not to change it, but to understand it, respect it, and reveal its full potential through every step of the process.”

— Sebastian Ramirez

products.title: COLOMBIA, Catalina Vasquez, Finca La Secreta, Bolivar, Antioquia
products.body_html:
Producer: Catalina Vasquez. 

Growing altitude: 1700-2050m above sea level.

Botanical variety: Caturra, Colombia.

Process: Washed.

Tasting notes: Molasses, vanilla, clove, mirabelle, orange, papaya flavours.

Roast date: 18 August, 2026

Antioquia is one of Colombia’s 32 departments, located in the country’s northwestern region, where the Andes mountain range stretches across dramatic valleys and mountainous terrain, with a narrow corridor reaching the Caribbean coastline. Nestled near the city of Ciudad Bolívar, Finca La Secreta sits within this rich and diverse landscape, an environment renowned for producing exceptional specialty coffee.

The farm spans more than 30 hectares, with 25 hectares dedicated to coffee cultivation and the remaining land preserved as protected natural reserve. The reserve is home to an abundance of native flora and wildlife, while the surrounding forests play a vital role in protecting the region’s water sources, supplying fresh water to the wider community around the farm.

At elevations reaching 1,950 meters above sea level, the combination of altitude, climate, and biodiversity creates ideal conditions for cultivating high-quality specialty coffee.

Traditionally, coffees from this region are processed using the fully washed method. After harvesting, the cherries are pulped and fermented overnight for approximately 12–18 hours. The coffee is then thoroughly washed, with immature beans carefully removed before drying begins. Drying typically takes between 8 and 15 days in traditional parabolic dryers — rustic structures fitted with transparent roofing that maximize heat retention and airflow, allowing for consistent drying even during overcast or rainy conditions while protecting the coffee from excessive direct exposure during peak sunlight hours.

products.title: EL SALVADOR, Baraona family, Los Pirineos, Berlin, Usulutan
products.body_html:
Producer: Diego Baraona.

Growing altitude: 1600m above sea level.

Botanical variety: Bourbon Elite.

Process: Natural.

Tasting notes: Dark chocolate, plum, melon, blackberry, kumquat fruit flavours.

Roast date: 27 August, 2026

Perched atop the Tepeca Volcano in Usulután, El Salvador, Los Pirineos is a farm with over 130 years of coffee heritage. Originally established in 1890, the farm has been in the Baraona family for generations. Today, it continues under the loving stewardship of Gilberto Baraona’s children, following his untimely passing.

Surrounded by the cities of Berlin, Santiago de María, and Jucuapa, Los Pirineos benefits from its location in a volcanic mountain range—known for nutrient-rich soils and ideal coffee-growing conditions. According to family history, the original seeds planted on the farm came from Antigua, Guatemala, laying the foundation for a legacy of quality.

Los Pirineos was one of the first farms in El Salvador to establish its own micro-mill, enabling full control over processing and consistent quality from lot to lot.

The farm is divided into small- to medium-sized plots, organised by varietal and location. Current cultivars include; Bourbon Elite, Pacas, Pacamara, Sudan Rume and Gesha. 

In partnership with Procafé, the farm also maintains experimental plots with a wide range of native varieties, natural mutants, and hybrids sourced from across the globe—making it a living laboratory of Salvadoran coffee diversity.

The post-harvest process at Los Pirineos is a blend of tradition, precision, and experimentation.

Selective Harvesting: Expert pickers are incentivised to pick only fully ripe cherries, which are delivered fresh to the mill each afternoon.

Sorting: Cherries are hand-sorted to remove underripes and overripe fruit before processing.

Eco-Pulping: Using Jotagallo eco-pulpers with mechanical demucilagers, skin, pulp, and about 70% of the mucilage are removed efficiently and cleanly.

Soaking & Washing: The parchment is then soaked overnight in clean water to improve clarity before being washed.

Drying: Coffees are sun-dried under shade on raised beds for 3 to 4 weeks, allowing for slow, even moisture reduction and full flavour development.

We’ve had the privilege of working with Los Pirineos for several years, purchasing a range of exceptional lots that showcase not just technical excellence, but deep family pride and commitment to quality.

“We couldn’t be more humbled to share the results of this family’s hard work. Every lot is a tribute to Gilberto’s legacy and the future his children continue to build.”

products.title: EL SALVADOR, Fernando Leto Escobar, El Cerro, Apaneca, Llamatepec
products.body_html:
Producer: Fernando Leto Escobar.

Growing altitude: 1500m above sea level.

Botanical variety: Pacas.

Process: Natural Dry Fermentation.

Tasting notes: Molasses, nougat, raspberry, apricot, gooseberry flavours.

Roast date: 27 August, 2026

Nestled in the eastern highlands of El Salvador, Finca El Cerro is the legacy of five generations of coffee producers. The Escobar family has been growing coffee for more than 150 years, cultivating deep knowledge, resilience, and a commitment to quality that spans lifetimes.

The farm is located at 1,500 meters above sea level in the world-renowned Apaneca-Ilamatepec coffee-growing region—surrounded by indigenous forests that create an ideal microclimate for producing exceptional coffee.

Today, Fernando Leto Escobar oversees the farm, carrying forward the vision of his late father, Don Fernando Sr., who entrusted him with the land and its legacy in 2016. Since taking the reins, Fernando has led the transformation of Finca El Cerro into a vertically integrated operation—managing coffee from tree to export.

In 2016, the farm established its own eco-friendly wet mill, giving Fernando and his team full control over processing and quality.

Finca El Cerro prioritizes environmental responsibility, with multiple zones transitioning to fully organic production. The team uses eco-conscious farming practices to reduce impact and improve soil health, ensuring long-term sustainability for both the land and the surrounding ecosystems.

The farm processes coffee using multiple methods, including Washed, Honey, Natural and more recently, experimental fermentations

One notable process is a dry fermentation method, where select, ripe cherries are first fermented in shaded tanks for 48 hours, Then, they are slow-dried on African raised beds over 30 days. First days in sun, to initiate drying, final days in shade, to slow it down and stabilise flavour development. 

Fernando and his team are actively experimenting with varietals, selecting only seeds from plants that show the best performance in both cup quality and agronomic traits.

One such variety is Pacas—a natural Bourbon mutation discovered in 1949 in Santa Ana, El Salvador. Like Caturra and Villa Sarchi, Pacas has a single-gene mutation that limits plant size. This dwarf stature allows for denser planting and increased yield per hectare, making it both efficient and high-potential in cup quality.

“Our family has been working this land for five generations, but every season still teaches us something new. We honor tradition, but we always look forward.”

— Fernando Leto Escobar

products.title: HELLO, my name is coffee.
products.body_html:
During the commissioning of our new roaster, we had to put Uyatshisha through her paces, running a few trial batches to dial in the magic. The result? Coffee that didn't quite make our QC cut, but still tastes far too good to waste. 

Think of it as our perfectly imperfect roast, still crafted from top quality beans, still ethically sourced, still paying producers fairly just with a few extra freckles of experimentation. 

It's better than supermarket coffee (by a long shot), and easier on the wallet.
